topic: Claude from zero: what Claude is, how it differs from ChatGPT, how to get it and what the plans cost, chat vs Cowork vs Claude Code, how to talk to it, what it is good and bad at, the words that matter, ten things to try in week one and a short test drive
audience: Complete beginners who have never opened Claude (or opened it once and closed it), including people coming from ChatGPT
goal: Get Claude on their devices on the right plan, set up the few settings that matter, brief it well, know what to check, and finish one real task in a ten-minute test drive
notes: Claude is a large language model (LLM) built by Anthropic, trained to be a helpful, honest and harmless assistant with a conversational tone. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude]

Anthropic describes itself as a Public Benefit Corporation whose mission is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. [https://www.anthropic.com/news]
You must be at least 18 years old to use Claude. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude]

Claude is only available in supported locations; the help-center list (dated March 16, 2026) includes Nigeria, the United Kingdom and the United States, among many others. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8461763-where-can-i-access-claude]

Where to get Claude: on the web at claude.ai; Claude Desktop for macOS, Windows and Linux (beta), downloaded from claude.com/download; Claude for iOS (App Store listing 'Claude by Anthropic') and Claude for Android. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10065433-install-claude-desktop] [https://claude.com/download]

Device requirements: macOS 13 (Ventura) or higher; Windows 10 or higher; Linux on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS+ or Debian 12+ (x64 or arm64); iOS and iPadOS 18.0 and above; Android 8.0 Oreo and above. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10065433-install-claude-desktop] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9266462-install-claude-for-ios] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9612887-install-claude-for-android]

The desktop and mobile apps are available on all plans including Free, and conversations, projects, memory and preferences sync across devices. In Claude Desktop, chat is on every plan including Free, while Claude Code and Claude Cowork need Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise. [https://claude.com/download] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10065433-install-claude-desktop]

Voice mode is a beta feature on all plans in Claude Mobile, Claude Desktop and the web, built to work best from a phone, with hands-free and push-to-talk modes; it counts toward usage limits. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11101966-use-voice-mode]

How to talk to Claude, from Anthropic's help center: speak to Claude like you would a coworker or friend, naturally and conversationally; prompts can range from simple questions to complex requests (multi-step projects, analysis, creative writing, coding or technical tasks). Type your prompt and click the submit button; click the '+' button in the lower left or type '/' to see more options and commands. Tips for getting started: start simple; be specific (the more specific your request, the better Claude can help); iterate (refine your prompts or ask follow-up questions); explore different types of tasks. Claude has extensive training in English and performs well in many other common languages. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude]

Anthropic's advice for handing Claude work: describe what you need the way you'd brief a colleague. You get better results when you include your desired outcome (what you want to end up with, like a one-page summary), the format (how you want it delivered, like a Word document, a slide deck or a message you can paste) and the inputs Claude will need (the files, links or apps to work from). Not sure where to start? Ask Claude what it can help with. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]

In the new Claude experience, chat and Cowork are merged into one conversation with no mode to choose: Claude can answer a quick question or take on research, reports, spreadsheets and presentations and hand them back as finished files. Hand Claude a whole task: describe the outcome you want and Claude works through the steps on its own, searching the web, reading your files, running code and putting the results together; more involved tasks keep running in the cloud if you close your laptop. Claude can create documents, spreadsheets with working formulas, and presentations you can open in PowerPoint. It is rolling out gradually to Pro, Max and Ultra on web, desktop and mobile; once an account moves, it can't switch back. Quick questions and longer tasks live together in Recents. There is no web search toggle (Claude searches the web when it helps); Research is under the '+' button below the chat input, or /deep-research. Instructions for every conversation are in Settings > Your Claude (Settings > Account in the older Settings layout). For work with real consequences, like sending messages or changing important files, stay close and review what Claude does. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]

Before the new experience reaches an account, you find the message box, select 'Cowork' in the bottom left corner and describe your task; to go back to a regular conversation, select 'Chat'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile]

Claude Cowork brings Claude Code's agentic capabilities to knowledge work beyond coding, using the same agentic architecture with no terminal required. Cowork is on paid plans only: Claude Desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux beta) on all paid plans; web and mobile on Pro, Max, Ultra and Team (beta on Team), and Enterprise when an owner enables it. Cowork runs sessions remotely in the cloud, so sessions and files follow your Claude account across desktop, web and mobile, and work continues when you close your laptop. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Anthropic warns that Cowork has unique risks because of its agentic nature and internet access, and that write tools carry more risk than read tools. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and integrates with development tools; it is available in the terminal, IDE, desktop app and browser. [https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview] Claude Code is included in all paid plans and shares the plan's usage limits with chat. [https://claude.com/pricing]

Claude in Chrome is a browser extension that lets Claude read, click and navigate websites; it is available on paid plans (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise). [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12012173-get-started-with-claude-in-chrome]
Claude for Microsoft 365 works inside Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook, generally available on all paid Claude plans. [https://claude.com/claude-for-microsoft-365]

Claude's pricing page lists six plans: Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise. Free costs $0 and includes limited usage every 5 hours and every week, chat on web, desktop and mobile, web search, file creation and code, memory, connectors, Artifacts, and Claude Design, Slides and Docs. [https://claude.com/pricing]

Pro costs $20 per month billed monthly, or $17 per month with the annual discount ($200 billed up front). Pro adds more usage, handing off and scheduling tasks, Claude Code, Projects, more Claude models, and Claude in Chrome and Microsoft 365. Pro is available monthly and annually; Max and Ultra are monthly only. [https://claude.com/pricing]

Max costs $100 per month and gives 5x Pro usage every 5 hours and every week, early access to features and priority access at high-traffic times. Ultra costs $200 per month and gives no 5-hour limit (for verified accounts) and 10x Pro usage every week. [https://claude.com/pricing] The Max 20x plan was renamed Ultra. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17728952-what-is-the-ultra-plan]

Team is for teams of 2 to 150: Standard seats cost $20 per seat/month billed annually or $25 monthly; Premium seats (5x Standard usage) cost $100 annually or $125 monthly. Team includes Claude Code and Cowork, admin controls and no model training on your content by default. Enterprise costs US$20 per seat per month billed annually with a 20-seat minimum, plus usage billed at API rates. [https://claude.com/pricing]

Listed prices exclude applicable tax, and Anthropic says prices and plans are subject to change. You can cancel any time in Settings > Billing; the plan stays active to the end of the billing period, and you should cancel at least 24 hours before renewal to avoid the next charge. [https://claude.com/pricing]
The help center lists Pro at $20 per month (US), with pricing in local currency where supported and a discounted annual option. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8325606-what-is-the-pro-plan]
The Pro plan does not include API usage through the Claude Console; API usage is paid separately. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8325606-what-is-the-pro-plan]

Free, Pro, Max and Ultra plans list model training as opt-out; Team and Enterprise list no model training on content by default. [https://claude.com/pricing] Whether your conversations are used to improve Claude follows the 'Help improve our AI models' setting in Settings > Privacy. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile] Anthropic's privacy center calls it Model Improvement in your Privacy Settings, and says incognito chats are not used to improve Claude even when it is on. [https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10023580-is-my-data-used-for-model-training]

Most accounts have a usage limit that resets on a rolling five-hour session window, paid plans add weekly limits, and use across web, desktop, mobile and Claude Code draws from one pool with no fixed message count. Pro gives more usage than Free (the pricing page says "More usage than Free"; Max is 5x Pro). [https://claude.com/pricing] The five-hour period starts with your first message and resets in full five hours later; remaining usage is shown under Current session in Settings > Usage. Weekly limits reset at a fixed day and time assigned to your account. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work] On the Free plan the number of messages varies with demand, and Claude tells you when you've reached your limit or when a prompt exceeds the available context window. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude]

Factors that use limits faster include message length, attachment size, conversation length, tool use (Research, web search), model choice, effort level, artifacts and multi-step tasks. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

The current models are Claude Fable 5.2 (demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work), Opus 5.5 (long-running agentic coding and knowledge work), Sonnet 5.5 (best combination of speed and intelligence) and Haiku 5.5 (high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks; latency 'Fastest'). If you're unsure which model to use, Anthropic's docs say start with Claude Opus 5.5. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview] On the Free plan, Sonnet and Haiku are available, but not Opus or Fable; Opus is on Pro, Max and Ultra. [https://claude.com/pricing]

The model menu next to the send button controls which model you chat with, the effort and thinking. The selected model shows next to the send button, below the text input, on web and desktop, and at the top of the screen on mobile; click the model name to switch, or click 'More models' for more options; changes apply from Claude's next response. Effort levels are Low, Medium, High, Extra high and Max; higher effort takes longer and uses more of your limits. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude] In the Claude apps the default effort is Medium. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5]

Training-data cutoffs: Fable 5.2, Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 run to June 2026. Models may not know about events after their training cutoff. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114494-how-up-to-date-is-claude-s-training-data]

In chat on paid plans, the newest models (Fable 5.2 and 5.1, Opus 5.5 and 5, Sonnet 5.5 and 5, Haiku 5.5) have 1M-token context windows; some older models have 500K, others 200K. A 200K context window means 200K+ tokens, about 500 pages of text or more. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8606394-how-large-is-the-context-window-on-paid-claude-plans]

Claude Fable and Claude Mythos are the same underlying model: Fable carries strong safeguards so it can be offered to all users, while Mythos is for verified organizations. Fable is on paid plans, not Free. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15424964-claude-fable-models-on-your-plan]

OpenAI's ChatGPT plans are Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise. ChatGPT Free advertises 'Unlimited text chats with GPT-6', subject to abuse guardrails. ChatGPT's plan table lists image generation on every plan (Limited on Free). ChatGPT's published context windows are 27K (Free), 54K (Go, Plus) and 128K (Pro) for GPT Instant, and 256K (Go, Plus) or 400K (Pro) for GPT Reasoning. [https://chatgpt.com/pricing/]

ChatGPT Plus costs $20/month billed monthly, the same as Claude Pro's monthly price. [https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6950777-what-is-chatgpt-plus] ChatGPT Pro comes in three monthly tiers: Pro 100 at $100, Pro 200 at $200 and Pro 500 at $500. [https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9793128-about-chatgpt-pro-tiers]

OpenAI says ads may appear in ChatGPT for Free and Go users (testing began in the US on February 9, 2026); Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu have no ads. [https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt] Anthropic committed on February 4, 2026 that Claude will remain ad-free, with no sponsored links and no advertiser influence on responses. [https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-is-a-space-to-think]

Claude does not generate photos or illustrations like image-generation tools; it builds diagrams, charts and interactive visuals with HTML and SVG, and can analyze images you upload. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9002504-can-claude-produce-images]

Conversation history from another AI provider cannot be imported into Claude; only memory can. To import memory, go to Settings > Your Claude and select 'Start import'; the import flow shows a prompt to use in your old service and a box to paste the result; paste it and click 'Add to memory'. Anthropic calls memory import experimental. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12123587-import-and-export-your-memory-from-claude] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude]

Projects are self-contained workspaces with their own chat histories and knowledge bases; they are available to all users, and Free users can create up to five. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects] To create a project, go to claude.ai/projects and click '+ New Project'; add files with '+' and instructions with 'Set project instructions'. Context is not shared across chats unless added to project knowledge. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects]

An artifact is anything Claude makes that you'd put in front of someone (a design, deck, document, dashboard or small interactive tool); it opens beside the conversation and can be edited and shared. Artifacts are on all plans. They need the 'Create and edit files' setting ('Code execution and file creation' in the older layout) on in Settings > Capabilities. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them]

Code execution and file creation is available to all users (Free through Enterprise) on web, desktop and mobile; Claude can generate Excel, PowerPoint, Word and PDF files, and it is on by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12111783-create-and-edit-files-with-claude]

Uploads: documents PDF, DOCX, CSV, TXT, HTML, ODT, RTF, EPUB, JSON and XLSX; images JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP; up to 500MB per file and 20 files per chat; PDFs up to 1000 pages. To upload, click the '+' button in the lower left corner of the chat box and select 'Add files or photos', or drag and drop files into the chat. Claude analyzes images and charts only in PDFs of 100 pages or fewer; for longer PDFs it reads the text only. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-upload-files-to-claude]

Web search: click the '+' button in the lower left corner of the chat window and click 'Web search' (a checkmark shows it's on); every answer includes citations so you can verify sources. In the new Claude experience there is no toggle and Claude searches when it helps. Free accounts can use it. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10684626-enable-and-use-web-search] Research (paid plans) runs multiple searches that build on each other across the web and connected tools, turned on with '+' > 'Research'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11088861-use-research-on-claude]

Connectors let Claude access your apps and services, retrieve data and take actions, inheriting each person's permissions; web connectors are available to all users. Browse them from a chat via '+' > 'Connectors' > 'Manage connectors', or from Customize > Connectors. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11176164-use-connectors-to-extend-claude-s-capabilities]

Memory is on by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra on web, desktop and mobile. Claude saves memory as individual topics as you chat, can be told to 'remember this', and keeps a separate memory for each project. You can see and edit what Claude remembers in Settings > Your Claude by selecting 'Manage' next to Your memory. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Incognito chats are opened with the ghost icon in the upper right corner when you start a new chat outside a project. They are not saved to chat history or memory and are not used for training, but are retained for 30 days by default; they are available on all plans. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12260368-use-incognito-chats]

Account-wide Instructions apply to all conversations: click your initials in the lower left corner, select Settings, then Your Claude (Account in the older Settings layout), and describe your instructions under Instructions. Project instructions apply within a project. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10185728-understanding-claude-s-personalization-features]

Settings sections named in Anthropic's help pages: General and Privacy [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile]; Your Claude [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10185728-understanding-claude-s-personalization-features]; Capabilities [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them]; Usage [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]; Billing [https://claude.com/pricing].

Claude can 'hallucinate' incorrect or misleading information; Anthropic says not to rely on it as a singular source of truth, to scrutinize high-stakes advice and to check cited sources. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8525154-claude-is-providing-incorrect-or-misleading-responses-what-s-going-on] Claude can also hallucinate its own capabilities, such as claiming to have sent emails; it has no access to tools that are not explicitly integrated. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241188-claude-is-producing-links-that-don-t-work-and-falsely-claiming-that-it-has-sent-emails-or-produced-external-documents-what-s-going-on]

Skills are folders of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads for specialized tasks; they are available on all plans. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512176-what-are-skills] Plugins bundle skills, connectors and sub-agents into one package, on all paid plans. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-claude]

Anthropic's Claude Academy offers courses such as Claude 101 (13 lessons, 1 quiz, 2.5 hours) and Claude Code 101 (12 lessons, 1 quiz, 1.5 hours), each with a completion badge. [https://academy.claude.com/courses]

About Mojeed: a data and AI leader and educator whose mission is to make data and AI easy for everyone; he teaches people to use AI at work; he founded DataGlobal Hub; he is a Forbes Technology Council member. Website: https://mojeedabisiga.com/ [https://mojeedabisiga.com/]

Logging in: on claude.ai, the desktop app or a mobile app you see two options, 'Continue with Google' (enter your Google email and password, click 'Next') or 'Continue with email' (enter your email; Claude sends an email with the subject 'Secure link to log in to Claude.ai' and a login link). Clicking the link on the same device logs you in; on a different device it generates a verification code to enter on the original device. If the login email hasn't arrived, check your spam and junk folders for emails from @mail.anthropic.com and try again after a few minutes. You can't create a dedicated password for a Claude account. If you're creating an account or logging in for the first time and see a message about your phone number, see 'Verifying your phone number'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13189465-log-in-to-your-claude-account]

Signing up for Pro: go to claude.ai, enter your email and click 'Continue with email' or click 'Continue with Google', use the emailed login link or the Google prompts, click your initials or name in the lower left corner and select 'Settings', go to Settings > Billing and click 'Upgrade plan', click 'Get Pro plan', choose monthly or annual billing, enter payment information and click 'Subscribe'. Pro renews automatically at the end of each billing period. Paid plans need you to be physically in a supported location, and creating an account needs a phone number from a supported location. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8325609-how-do-i-sign-up-for-the-pro-plan]

Settings > Usage on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and seat-based Enterprise shows progress bars: the 'Plan usage limits' section at the top shows 'Current session' (how much of the five-hour session limit you've used plus time remaining) and 'Weekly limits' (when the weekly limit resets, for all models and for Fable if your plan includes it); a 'Usage credits' section appears on paid plans. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices] Usage credits let Pro, Max and Ultra keep working after limits at standard API rates, turned on in Settings > Usage with a monthly spend limit. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-manage-usage-credits-for-paid-claude-plans] A limit reset restores a five-hour, weekly or Fable limit via 'Reset for free' in Settings > Usage. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17007452-what-is-a-limit-reset]

Creating a project: hover over the left side and click 'Projects' (or go to claude.ai/projects), click '+ New Project' in the upper right corner, give it a name and description (Claude does not see these). The project knowledge base is on the right of the project page: click '+' to upload documents, text or code. Click 'Set project instructions', add how Claude should behave and click 'Save instructions'; they apply to all chats in the project. Context is not shared across chats in a project unless it is in project knowledge. On paid plans project knowledge switches to RAG near the context limit, expanding capacity by up to 10x. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects] Project content is cached and counts less against limits when reused. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

Model menu details: to change effort, click the model name next to the send button, click 'Effort' and choose a level; each model's recommended level is marked 'Default'. Low and Medium work well for routine tasks and stretch usage further; High offers the best balance of quality and speed; Extra high is for long-running coding and agentic tasks; Max is the most thorough. For everyday tasks the defaults work well. Thinking can't be turned off on Fable 5.2, Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 or Opus 5; choose a lower effort to make Claude think less. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings] Latency: Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 'Moderate', Sonnet 5.5 'Fast', Haiku 5.5 'Fastest'. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview] Anthropic positions Sonnet 5.5 as strongest at well-scoped everyday tasks and polished documents, slides and spreadsheets, and Opus 5.5 for complex work needing careful judgment. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5] For chat users, Anthropic recommends Haiku or the most recent Sonnet for most tasks because they cost fewer tokens than Opus. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-manage-usage-credits-for-paid-claude-plans]
Training-data cutoffs of older models: Opus 5 to May 2026; Sonnet 5 and Fable 5 to January 2026. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114494-how-up-to-date-is-claude-s-training-data]

Web search vs Research: web search suits factual queries that need one or two searches; Research suits information gathering that needs five or more over 1 to 3 minutes. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11095361-when-should-i-use-web-search-extended-thinking-and-research] Research runs on Opus 5.5 whatever model the chat uses; Research started in Claude Mobile only searches the web and skips connectors. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11088861-use-research-on-claude] A link to a long article pulls the whole article into Claude's context and uses more of your limit; Anthropic suggests asking Claude not to search the web when you don't need current information and turning off connected apps a chat doesn't need. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10684626-enable-and-use-web-search] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

Custom visuals: Claude can draw diagrams, charts and interactive visuals inline in a chat (beta, all users, web and desktop; not rendered in the iOS or Android apps). Nothing needs turning on: ask with phrases like 'draw this as a diagram' or 'chart this data'. They are temporary by default; keep one with Copy as image, Download (.svg or .html) or Save as artifact. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13979539-custom-visuals-in-chat-and-cowork]

Files and artifacts: Claude creates Excel (.xlsx), PowerPoint (.pptx), Word (.docx) and PDF files in a conversation; you download them or save them directly to Google Drive; you ask in plain language, for example 'Convert this document into a PowerPoint presentation'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12111783-create-and-edit-files-with-claude] Anthropic's built-in skills handle Excel, Word, PowerPoint and PDF creation and are used automatically. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude] Artifact templates: Docs, Slides and Design on all plans; Data on paid plans; Sheets and Whiteboards in beta on paid plans. Claude Slides can be edited slide by slide, presented inside Claude and exported to PowerPoint or PDF. For template artifacts, 'Export' sends docs to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs and decks to PowerPoint, PDF or Google Slides. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them] Artifacts start private; to share, open it, click 'Share', choose who can open it under 'Who has access', copy the link. The help-center table gives link sharing to Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise (claude.com's Artifacts page also lists Free). [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9547008-share-artifacts]

Claude for Excel answers questions about a workbook with cell-level citations, adjusts assumptions while keeping formulas intact, debugs errors and builds models; it runs on Excel on the web, Windows (Microsoft 365 build 16.0.13127.20296 or later) and Mac 16.46 or later. [https://claude.com/docs/office-agents/excel] In Outlook, Claude's drafts and calendar invites open in Outlook's compose form and wait for you to click send; in Word, Claude edits with tracked changes. [https://claude.com/claude-for-microsoft-365] Claude for PowerPoint builds slides in your templates, makes pinpoint edits and turns bullets into diagrams and native PowerPoint charts; it reads the slide master, layouts, fonts and colours; its charts and diagrams are editable. The add-ins are installed from the 'Claude for Microsoft 365' listing on Microsoft AppSource ('Get it now'), activated from Home > Add-ins (Windows) or Tools > Add-ins (Mac), then you sign in with your Claude account. [https://claude.com/docs/office-agents/powerpoint]

Scheduled tasks (all paid plans, in Cowork and the new Claude experience) run a saved prompt on a schedule or on demand. In the new experience you describe the task and how often in any conversation, review Claude's proposal and click 'Schedule'; you can also click 'Scheduled' in the left sidebar or type /schedule. Frequencies: hourly, daily, weekly, on weekdays or manually. They run remotely, even when your computer is asleep, unless you pick a folder ('Require this computer'). Safety advice: start simple, avoid sensitive data and hard-to-undo actions, review outputs after each run, pause tasks you're not using. You remain responsible for actions Claude takes on your behalf. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

Cowork's intended workflow: describe an outcome, step away, and come back to finished work such as formatted documents, organized files and synthesized research; it can produce Excel spreadsheets with working formulas, PowerPoint presentations and formatted documents. Multi-step tasks use more usage than a quick question. Official tips: group related work into one task, start a new conversation for unrelated work, tell Claude when you only need a quick answer, and check Settings > Usage. Anthropic notes the automatic approval check can miss risky actions; for money, messages sent as you or important files, stay close or switch to 'Manually approve'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Usage tips from Anthropic: combine related questions in one message and give background up front, be specific and concise, batch similar requests, review your prompt before sending; in a long chat near your limit, start a new conversation; keep project instructions short, remove unused project files and use a lower effort for routine tasks. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

Prompting advice from Anthropic: treat Claude like a brilliant but new employee who lacks context on your norms; the key test is whether a colleague with minimal context could follow your prompt; be specific about format and constraints and ask explicitly if you want more than the minimum; give the reason behind an instruction; tell Claude what to do rather than what not to do; with long documents, put the documents first and the question at the end (Anthropic says up to 30% better quality in tests). [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices] Start with one example and add more only if needed; longer prompts are not always better and the first prompt rarely works perfectly. [https://claude.com/resources/articles/best-practices-for-prompt-engineering] To reduce hallucinations, give Claude permission to say 'I don't know', and for long documents ask for word-for-word quotes first and to back each claim with a quote or retract it; this reduces but doesn't eliminate them. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations]

Searching past chats is on paid plans and can be switched off at Settings > Your Claude > 'Search and reference chats'. Memory is shared between chat and Cowork when Cowork runs in the cloud. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Computer use (Claude clicking, typing and opening apps on your screen) is on Pro, Max and Ultra in Cowork and Claude Code in Claude Desktop for macOS and Windows. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14128542-let-claude-use-your-computer-in-cowork] Claude in Chrome waits for you on purchases, financial actions and anything irreversible, and Anthropic advises skipping banking, health records and credential workflows. [https://claude.com/claude-in-chrome]
